report.title: 2025 Water Quality Consumer Confidence Report (Published June 2026)

sources_described: Three water sources used interchangeably or blended: protected groundwater wells within Santa Clara (20 active wells, 500-900 feet deep, supplying most of the water), Sierra Nevada snowmelt via the SFPUC Hetch Hetchy System (typically serving the area north of Highway 101; fluoridated), and Valley Water treated surface water from the Rinconada Water Treatment Plant (Calero Reservoir and Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta imports; serving primarily the south-west portion of the City). Together they provide an average of 15 million gallons per day.

violations: Tier 3 Notice from SFPUC (PDF page 5): The SFPUC notified the City of a monitoring violation, as is required within one year of discovery. Because of equipment failure, the San Francisco Regional Water System (SFRWS) operated by the SFPUC did not monitor for recycled filter backwash water turbidity at its Sunol Valley Water Treatment Plant (SVWTP) from June 23 to July 2, 2025. It was corrected July 3, 2025, once it became apparent to plant staff. There was no emergency or impact to SFPUC's water quality; downstream monitoring indicated SVWTP effluent was consistently of very high quality and exceeded all drinking water standards.

Lead (PDF page 5): 'No Santa Clara water sources have exceeded the ACTION LEVEL for lead.' Residential-tap sampling (52 taps, 2022): lead 90th percentile ND, 0 exceedances; copper 90th percentile 0.34 ppm, 0 exceedances.

School lead testing 2018 (PDF page 4 table, note 6): 33 schools, 172 samples; 90th percentile ND; Number Exceeded = 1 - the 2018 sampling result for John Sutter Elementary was 26 ppb; repeat sampling following plumbing repairs was non-detect for lead.

Report states all water meets applicable drinking water standards; only constituents detected in at least one water source appear in the table. Hexavalent chromium: all 20 groundwater wells tested below the 10 ppb MCL (PDF page 6).
extraction_notes: The water quality table is PDF page 4 of the 6-page report; the city also publishes it as a separate 1-page accessible PDF (reports/CA4310012/ccr-2025-water-quality-table.pdf) with identical content, which was used to cross-check. Source columns are 'CSC WELL WATER', 'VALLEY WATER' and 'SFPUC', each printed Range then Average; the SFPUC header adds '[highest running average]'. Standards columns are 'MCL' and 'State PHG/Fed MCLG' for source-water rows ('NS' = no standard for Consumer Information rows). The distribution-system table (coliform, E. coli, TTHM, HAA5, chlorine residual, lead, copper, lithium) has no source columns, so source_group is null; its second standards column is headed 'State MCL' and holds PHG/MRDLG-type values (0.3, 0.2, 4) which were stored as phg_printed; for Total Coliform that column (5.0%) was not stored as a PHG. Cells printed 'NA' have no entry (Giardia, gross alpha, uranium, bicarbonate, boron, chlorate, phosphate, silica, TOC and vanadium for well water; nitrate+nitrite, pH, temperature, vanadium for SFPUC; chlorate for Valley Water). Where the average is printed ND but the range shows a detection (e.g. 'ND - 0.21'), detected=true, value=range high, average=null. Values printed with '<' (e.g. '< 3 - 11', '<5', '< 20') keep the numeral in range_low with a note; cells where both range and average are '<x' are detected=false. Foaming Agents (MBAS) is printed in PPB with values 0.022/0.014 against an MCL of 500 (probable ppm/ppb inconsistency, kept as printed). Lead/copper residential-tap sampling is dated 2022 and school lead testing 2018 by the table itself; all other rows carry sample_year 2025 (the report's data year) although the report says some data may be more than one year old. Lithium table range 'ND - 10' conflicts with the page-5 narrative that lithium was not detected under UCMR5. PFAS entries (page 5) come from the UCMR5 narrative, not from a table, and carry no units or limits. pdftotext -layout jumbled the Chlorate/Hardness rows; they were reconstructed from word coordinates (pdftotext -bbox-layout) and match the separate table PDF.
